full_judgment:
The pre-emptor filed the pre-emption Case No. 37 of 2003 before the Assistant Judge, Wazirpur, Barisal under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act against the opposite parties stating that father of the pre-emptor was the owner of one acre of land in SA Khatian Nos. 724, 730 and 589 and the same has been recorded in his name and he has been died during the possession of the case land. The father of the pre-emptor died leaving behind his one son Taib Ali (pre-emptor) and five daughters. One son gets 28 decimals of land and one daughter gets 14 decimals of land. The first daughter transferred her land to the pre-emptee No. 8 by her deed dated 3-11-99. Daughter Hachenbhanu transferred her land to the Pre-emptee Nos. 6 and 7 by her deed dated 17-4.94. Daughter Khatunbhanu transferred her land to the pre-emptor Taib Ali Mridha and Meher Nega is the pre-emptee No. 9. The heirs of the pre-emptor and purchasers are possession in total 42 decimals of land of three khatians. Shohorbhanu died leaving behind her three sons and one daughter and they have been owner of the 14 decimals land and they are the pre-emptee Nos. 2-5 of the instant case and they are also nephews of the pre-emptor. On 23-4-2003 the sellers transferred 15 decimals of land to the pre-emptee No.1 (purchaser) by registered deed is valued in cash of Taka 98,000. In the meantime the pre-emptor did not know about the matter. On 3-5-2003 at first the pre-emptor knew the facts through A. Karim. On 6-5-2003 the pre-emptor searched the Wazirpur Sub-Registry office and obtained the certified copy of the kabala. The pre-emptor is a co-sharer by inheritance of the jama. The Kabala purchaser No.1 is a stranger and no notice has been served upon the pre-emptor and he did not know at al. The pre-emptor cultivated three biggas land and the said land is the homestead of the pre-emptor. Hence, this case. 

 4. The pre-emptee petitioner contested the case by filing a written statement denying the material allegations made in the pre-emption case contending, Inter alia, that the kabala seller Nos. 2-5 are nephews of the sister of pre-emptor and the schedule land is the ejmali land. If the pre-emptee is the co-sharers of the land but they had no physical possession in the said land. The pre-emptor and the co-sharers are possession in the said land. The opposite party Nos. 2-5 are the residents of Char Mojanpur and Boradi Gorail under the Police Station Gourabnadi. When they knew their uncle (pre-emptor) Taib Ali for selling their land then he did not buy their land. Thereafter the kabala seller pre-emptees sold their land to the kabala purchaser pre-emptee. When the seller asked the pre-emptee then he did not agree for selling their land. A Karim Sarder and Hochen Howlader are the relative of the pre-emptor and they are same party and they are also false statements before this Court and as such the pre-emption case is liable to be dismissed. 

 17. On perusal of the records, it appears that the pre-emptee-petitioner in his written objection mentioned that when the pre-emptor-opposite party was informed about the sale of the suit land, he expressed his reluctance to purchase it. Since the pre-emptor-opposite party expressed his reluctance, the land under suit deed was purchased by the pre-emptee-petitioner and OPW Nos.1-3 also categorically stated that before selling of the suit land, they informed about it to the pre-emptee-opposite parties who is their maternal uncle but he denied to purchase the suit land. It is interesting to mention here that the pre-emptor-opposite party is the only maternal uncle and the guardians of the OPW Nos.1-3. Therefore, it is unreasonable that OPW Nos.1-3 would sell the land inherited from their mother without asking their uncle.
